payload.name: Preference-to-Shop Inference from Named Collection Items
payload.description: When a question asks what shop or venue a person would enjoy based on collections or interests, and retrieval surfaces a named item/creator/prop, use general knowledge linking that item to a real shop or venue.
content: When asked for a shop or place a person would enjoy visiting based on collections or interests, first search for the person's collection/preference memories using terms like collection, prop, item, favorite, enjoys, and any named entities from the question; do not restrict queries to location-plus-shop phrasing.

If a retrieved memory names a specific creator, prop, or branded item, use general world knowledge to identify a real shop or venue associated with that item (e.g., a creator's official store) and treat that as evidence the person would enjoy visiting it, even if the memory does not name the shop.
Answer with the shop or venue only when the person's stated preference aligns with its known offerings; stop after one preference-retrieval pass and one alignment judgment to avoid over-searching.

solves: When an access question asks for a shop or venue a person would enjoy based on their collections or interests, retrieval may miss the decisive memory if it only mentions a named item, creator, or prop without location or shop terms. The agent may then guess from a loosely related plan. This Skill guides retrieval of collection/preference memories using named entities, and inference to the associated real-world shop or venue.
